newsitem.title: USA: US House tax conferees send Senate offer.
newsitem.headline: US House tax conferees send Senate offer.

text.p: House lawmakers negotiating the tax bill agreed Tuesday to send their Senate counterparts a first offer, but major issues remained unresolved, House Ways and Means Committee Chairman Bill Archer said.

"There are a lot of major issues still unresolved," the Texas Republican told reporters after a meeting of House tax conferees. The House tax group planned to send the Senate two documents, he said. "The first document is to approve the identical provisions" or very similar ones that have been looked over by Republican, Democratic and White House staff, Archer said. "So there should be no question about those."

"Then we get into some (issues) that are not similar, many of which have also been looked at by bipartisan staff and the White House, and we include an effort to resolve those in the second document," Archer said.

The House conferees will now wait for the Senate to respond. The tax conferees are trying to work out the differences in their separate tax legislation so Congress can eventually vote on one final bill.
Archer said at this point the House offer did not attempt to resolve the differences in proposed international arrival and departure fees for airline passengers.
"We have not at this point attempted to resolve that," Archer said. He has previously said the provision in the House bill for a $15.50 per passenger departure and arrival fee was too high.
